tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves.summary: Neither library contains the Katz–Mazur theory itself: there are no elliptic curves over a base scheme, no Weierstrass model scheme, no Drinfeld or naive level structures, no moduli problems over Ell, no p-divisible groups or Serre–Tate theory, and no coarse or compactified modular curves. What exists is foundational or equation-level: Mathlib has affine group schemes, the flat rank, descent of morphisms along fpqc and fppf covers, relative normalisation with smooth base change, finiteness from proper plus quasi-finite, and the classification by j over separably closed fields. Tau Ceti has Cartier duality over an affine base, constant and diagonalizable group schemes, fppf quotient sheaves, and equation-level isogenies including deg [N] = N² (which the roadmap believes is not yet exported), E(K) ≅ Cl⁰ over a field, and connectedness under algebraically closed field extension (the roadmap's external contract (i) in 5C). Genuinely missing is everything scheme-theoretic over a general base: relative Cartier divisors, Weil restriction and relative Grassmannians, effective descent of objects, the relative cohomology of 𝒪_E(n[0]), the scheme group law, quotients, duals and the Weil pairing of elliptic curves, and all of the Katz–Mazur moduli theory built on them (level structures, regularity, cyclicity, quotients, and coarse and compactified curves).

targets.target: 0B: affine group schemes over Spec R anti-equivalent to commutative Hopf algebras
targets.note: Mathlib's Group/Affine.lean and Tau Ceti's assembled equivalence. Details under 0B.

targets.target: 0C: A is integral over A^G for a finite group G
targets.note: Details under 0C.

targets.target: 0D: étale cancellation and local constancy of the rank of finite locally free morphisms
targets.note: Details under 0D.

targets.target: 0E: descent of sections and morphisms along fpqc and fppf covers
targets.note: Subcanonical topologies and effective epimorphisms. Details under 0E.

targets.target: 0A: relative effective Cartier divisors on smooth relative curves, with fibre criterion, sections, sums, degree, incidence loci and the subgroup criterion
targets.note: No effective Cartier divisor exists in either library; only generic inputs (finite ⇔ proper and quasi-finite, locally constant rank, flatness of B/(g)) are present. Details under 0A.

targets.target: 0B: finite locally free commutative group schemes over a general base, kernels, fppf quotients, constant and diagonalizable groups, Cartier duality, (ℤ/N)ᴰ ≅ μ_N, killing by the rank
targets.note: Over an affine base Tau Ceti has Cartier duality with biduality and base change, constant groups, μ_n = D(ℤ/n), kernels and fppf quotient sheaves. Missing: the non-affine base, representability of quotients, exactness, the duality (ℤ/N)ᴰ ≅ μ_N and Deligne's theorem. Details under 0B.

targets.target: 0C: affine quotients by finite groups with universal property and finiteness, finite group-scheme torsors, SGA 3 V 4.1 quotients by finite locally free equivalence relations
targets.note: Module-finiteness is a composition of Mathlib lemmas; there are no scheme quotients. Details under 0C.

targets.target: 0D: finite étale K-schemes ≃ finite continuous Galois sets, with transport of group objects and pairings; sections, fibre counts and descent
targets.note: Only the separably closed case of the equivalence exists. Details under 0D.

targets.target: 0E: effective descent of the listed objects, including polarised projective curves, and spreading out
targets.note: Morphisms spread out and descend; objects do not. Details under 0E.

targets.target: 0F: Weil restriction along finite locally free maps and the Hom-schemes it represents
targets.note: Details under 0F.

targets.target: 0G: the relative Grassmannian and the parameter scheme of rank-N subgroup schemes
targets.note: Only the Grassmannian functor exists; its representability is a Mathlib TODO. Details under 0G.

duplicates.note: Owns étale equivalence-relation quotients and effective descent for sheaves, finite flat groups, polarisations and projective objects: most of 0C and 0E in general form.
Owns Cartier duality and finite-flat subgroup and quotient constructions, the general theory behind 0B.
Owns Weil restriction along finite locally free base maps (0F).
Owns the relative Grassmannian and closedness of invariant-subbundle equations (0G).
Owns relative effective Cartier divisors (0A).
Owns the Galois-category equivalence for finite étale covers (0D).

targets.target: Relative effective Cartier divisor on C/S: an effective Cartier divisor whose closed subscheme is flat over S, as the one shared carrier
targets.note: Tau Ceti's CartierDivisor is the group of global sections of 𝒦ˣ/𝒪ˣ on an integral scheme: absolute, not effective, and not flat over a base. Mathlib has ideal sheaves and closed subschemes but no invertible-ideal (effective Cartier) predicate, absolute or relative.

targets.target: Fibre criterion: over a locally noetherian S, with C/S flat and locally of finite type and D ⊆ C closed, finitely presented and S-flat, D is relative effective Cartier iff every geometric fibre is; plus the limit/descent version
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves the algebraic slicing step: if B is R-flat and g acts injectively on (R/I) ⊗ B for every finitely generated ideal I, then B/(g) is R-flat. Missing: the local criterion for flatness that reduces this to geometric fibres, the scheme-level statement and the limit version.

targets.target: A section P : S ⟶ C of a separated smooth relative curve defines the relative effective Cartier divisor [P]
targets.note: Only the closed-image half is in Mathlib: if f ≫ g is a closed immersion and g is separated then f is one, so a section of a separated morphism is a closed immersion. Missing: invertibility of its ideal sheaf in the smooth relative curve and flatness of degree one over S.

targets.target: Sums, inverse images under flat morphisms, and arbitrary base change preserve relative effective Cartier divisors
targets.note: There is no carrier, so none of the stability statements exists.

targets.target: A relative effective Cartier divisor is finite over S iff it is proper over S, and is then finite locally free
targets.note: Mathlib proves finite ⇔ proper and locally quasi-finite for any morphism (Stacks 02LS). Missing: quasi-finiteness of a relative Cartier divisor on a relative curve, and the conclusion that it is finite locally free.

targets.target: Degree of a divisor as the locally constant rank of the finite locally free morphism; inverse images under finite flat maps of curves multiply degrees
targets.note: Mathlib has the rank function of a finite flat morphism, its local constancy under local finite presentation, its invariance under base change, and multiplicativity of stalk ranks for tensor products in a tower. There is no degree of a divisor and no multiplicativity of Hom.finrank along a composite (FlatRank.lean has only composition with an isomorphism).

targets.target: Universal incidence locus D′ ≤ D and equality locus D′ = D: scheme structures, universal properties, base change
targets.note: Neither library represents containment or equality of closed subschemes.

targets.target: Subgroup criterion for a finite locally free divisor on a commutative smooth relative curve, in terms of identity, inversion and addition
targets.note: No group-scheme statement about divisors exists. Tau Ceti's ClosedSubgroupScheme is only a closed-immersion subobject of a group object.

duplicates.note: Lists relative effective Cartier divisors (with symmetric powers) as its own target; 0A says to use that shared definition and adds only the KM-specific lemmas.
Proves that a section through the relative smooth locus, and a sum of disjoint such sections, is an effective Cartier divisor compatibly with base change (0A items 2–3).

targets.target: Affine group schemes over Spec R anti-equivalent to commutative Hopf algebras (consumed from Group/Affine.lean)
targets.note: Mathlib has hopfSpec fully faithful with essential image the affine group schemes, as the roadmap says. Tau Ceti assembles these into the equivalence (CommHopfAlgCat R)ᵒᵖ ≌ AffineGroupSchemeCat.

targets.target: The category of finite locally free (finite, flat, locally finitely presented) commutative group schemes over S
targets.note: Tau Ceti has this category over an affine base Spec R, with finiteness, flatness, local finite presentation and commutativity built in. Missing: the category over an arbitrary base scheme S, which the roadmap uses throughout.

targets.target: Scheme-theoretic kernel of an arbitrary homomorphism, with base change (and no claim that it is finite locally free)
targets.note: For affine group schemes over Spec R, Tau Ceti builds the kernel as the closed subgroup cut out by the kernel Hopf ideal, with the pullback square against the identity section and coordinate ring K ⊗_H R. The kernel of a central isogeny over a noetherian base is shown finite locally free. Missing: kernels of homomorphisms of non-affine group schemes (such as E ⟶ E′) over a general base, and a base-change theorem for them.

targets.target: fppf quotient G/C by a closed finite locally free subgroup, representable under 0C's hypotheses, with an fppf-exact sequence
targets.note: Over an affine base Tau Ceti builds the fppf quotient sheaf of an affine group by a closed normal subgroup, with its universal property, local surjectivity of the projection and the torsor kernel pair; it asserts no representability. Missing: a scheme representing G/C, and exactness over a non-affine base.

targets.target: Constant finite group scheme G_S = ⨆_{g∈G} S ≅ Spec ∏ 𝒪_S, with coordinate algebra Map(G,R) over Spec R
targets.note: Over Spec R and for a finite group G, Tau Ceti has the constant group scheme, its coordinate ring identified with functions G → R, and finiteness and étaleness. Missing: the construction over a non-affine base S and its description as the coproduct ⨆_{g∈G} S.

targets.target: Diagonalizable group scheme D_S(M) = Spec 𝒪_S[M], and μ_N = D_S(ℤ/N)
targets.note: Over Spec R Tau Ceti defines D(M) for a finitely generated abelian group M, and μ_n as D(ℤ/n) with points the n-th roots of unity. Missing: the relative spectrum 𝒪_S[M] over a non-affine base S.

targets.target: Cartier duality as an anti-equivalence on finite locally free commutative group schemes, with evaluation, biduality, rank and base change
targets.note: Complete over an affine base Spec R: the anti-equivalence, natural biduality G ≅ D(D(G)), and compatibility with base change along R ⟶ S. The index drops the TauCeti. prefix of the first two names. Missing: duality over a non-affine base, a stated preservation of rank, and the evaluation pairing G × Gᴰ ⟶ 𝔾ₘ as a morphism.

targets.target: Exactness of Cartier duality on fppf-exact sequences of finite locally free groups; kernel–quotient comparison
targets.note: Neither library has fppf-exact sequences of finite flat group schemes or an exactness statement for duality. Tau Ceti's exact sequences in the algebraic-group library are group extensions of points and conormal sequences.

targets.target: ((ℤ/N)_S)ᴰ ≅ μ_N and (μ_N)ᴰ ≅ (ℤ/N)_S
targets.note: Both sides exist over Spec R, and the constant group's coordinate ring is defined as the linear dual of the group algebra R[G], so the identification reduces to the double-dual isomorphism evalIso. Neither isomorphism is stated, and the constant group is not placed in the finite locally free commutative category.

targets.target: A finite locally free commutative group scheme of rank N is killed by N (Deligne)
targets.note: No statement about multiplication by the rank on a finite flat group scheme exists (searched: killed, Deligne, Oort, annihilat).

duplicates.note: Develops Cartier duality, finite-flat subgroup and quotient constructions and fpqc descent for finite flat group schemes, the general theory 0B specialises.
Owns D(M) and μ_n = D(ℤ/n), and names Cartier duality of finite locally free commutative group schemes as a separate target; Tau Ceti's affine-base Cartier duality was built against this layer.
Owns kernels and the fppf sheaf quotient G/H, with representability as a separate theorem; Tau Ceti's kernelSpec and fppfQuotientSheaf were built against it.

targets.target: Affine quotient Spec A^G by a finite group acting on Spec A, with its categorical universal property among schemes
targets.note: Mathlib has the invariant subalgebra, but no scheme quotient by a group action and no universal property of Spec A^G (searched: categorical quotient, geometric quotient, quotient by a finite group).

targets.target: A is integral over A^G for a finite group G
targets.note: For a finite group G acting on B and any A ⟶ B whose image contains the fixed points, B is integral over A. With A the invariant subalgebra the hypothesis holds by definition.

targets.target: If A is of finite type over an invariant base ring and G acts by base-algebra automorphisms, A is module-finite over A^G, so the quotient map is finite
targets.note: Not stated, but a three-step composition in Mathlib: integrality over A^G, finite type over A^G by the tower lemma, and integral plus finite type gives module-finite. Tau Ceti proves only the case of a group algebra over a Galois extension of fields.

targets.target: Finite locally free group-scheme torsors on affine schemes: Hopf–Galois criterion, invariant algebra, faithful flatness, descent, affine fppf quotient with universal property
targets.note: No Hopf–Galois extension, comodule algebra or general torsor notion exists. The Tau Ceti torsor square concerns an affine group modulo a closed normal subgroup, not a group scheme acting on an arbitrary affine scheme.

targets.target: SGA 3 V 4.1, affine case: a finite locally free equivalence relation R ⇉ X on affine X has an affine quotient X/R, X ⟶ X/R finite locally free surjective, R = X ×_{X/R} X, representing the fppf quotient sheaf
targets.note: No quotient by an equivalence relation in schemes exists. Mathlib only has Zariski-local representability of a sheaf covered by relatively representable open immersions, which is the gluing input.

targets.target: Free action of a finite constant group with an invariant affine open cover: glue the affine invariant quotients and represent the fppf quotient; verify the hypothesis for the moduli schemes of Layers 4, 5 and 9
targets.note: Nothing about free group actions on schemes or their quotients exists in either library.

duplicates.note: Constructs quotients by étale equivalence relations and is asked to compare them with this roadmap's finite étale quotient construction; overlaps item 3.
Owns finite-flat subgroup and quotient constructions with fpqc descent, which overlap the finite-group-scheme torsor quotients of item 2.
Owns the fppf sheaf quotient of a group scheme and its representability under hypotheses, the group case of item 2's torsor quotient.

targets.target: Cancellation for étale morphisms
targets.note: Mathlib: if f ≫ g is étale and g is unramified and locally of finite type, then f is étale.

targets.target: Local constancy of the degree of a finite étale (finite locally free) morphism
targets.note: The rank of any finite flat morphism locally of finite presentation is locally constant; finite étale morphisms satisfy these hypotheses.

targets.target: Sections of finite étale morphisms (open and closed immersions)
targets.note: Mathlib has the two ingredients: the diagonal of an unramified morphism of finite type is an open immersion, and a section of a separated morphism is a closed immersion. That a section of a finite étale morphism is open and closed is not stated.

targets.target: Fibre cardinalities: a finite étale morphism of rank n has n points in each geometric fibre
targets.note: Over a separably closed field Mathlib proves a finite étale algebra is a finite product of copies of the field, and that étale algebras over any field are finite products of finite separable extensions. The scheme-level fibre count is not stated.

targets.target: Descent for finite étale schemes along fpqc covers
targets.note: Being étale descends along quasi-compact flat surjections, and along faithfully flat ring maps. Effective descent of the finite étale scheme itself is missing (Mathlib's Descent.lean lists descent of affine morphisms as a TODO).

targets.target: Over a field K, the equivalence between finite étale K-schemes and finite continuous Gal(Kˢ/K)-sets
targets.note: Only the separably closed case is proved: finite étale Ω-algebras are anti-equivalent to finite sets. Mathlib's Galois-category theorem gives an equivalence with finite continuous Aut(F)-sets for any Galois category, but finite étale K-algebras are not shown to form one, and Aut of the fibre functor is not identified with Gal(Kˢ/K).

targets.target: The equivalence preserves products and transports group objects, commutative group objects, homomorphisms and alternating pairings
targets.note: Depends on the equivalence above; no transport of group objects or pairings exists.

duplicates.note: Constructs the automorphism group of the geometric fibre functor on finite étale covers with its equivalence to finite continuous sets, recovering the absolute Galois group for Spec K: the general form of 0D's equivalence.

targets.target: Effective faithfully flat descent, with cocycle and uniqueness, for affine schemes
targets.note: Mathlib proves that extension of scalars along a faithfully flat ring map is comonadic, the Amitsur equalizer A = eq(B ⇉ B ⊗_A B), and the general IsStack formalism. Its own docstring leaves effective descent for modules as a TODO, and no stack instance for affine schemes or algebras exists.

targets.target: Descent of sections and morphisms along fpqc and fppf covers
targets.note: Mathlib proves that the fpqc and fppf topologies are subcanonical, and that quasi-compact flat surjections and fppf surjections are effective epimorphisms. So morphisms and sections that agree on overlaps descend uniquely. The four instances are unnamed in the source; their generated names were confirmed with Lean.

targets.target: Effective descent for finite locally free schemes, closed subschemes, finite locally free subgroup schemes and Cartier-divisor equalities
targets.note: Mathlib descends properties of morphisms (isomorphism, open immersion, universally closed and open), not objects. No effective descent of schemes or subschemes exists.

targets.target: Effective descent of projective relative curves equipped with a compatibly descended relatively ample line bundle
targets.note: Neither library defines relative ampleness or polarised descent.

targets.target: Descent of group objects, homomorphisms, the group law and its axioms, level structures, finite group actions and torsors
targets.note: Once the scheme has descended, the group law descends by descent of morphisms (above) and its axioms by faithfulness of pullback along fpqc covers, which Mathlib proves. Tau Ceti describes the points of an affine group by faithfully flat descent. Level structures, actions and torsors have no descent statement.

targets.target: Spreading out: finite-presentation models for a polarised curve with section, group law, subgroup and level data; morphisms and equalities descend to a common finite stage
targets.note: For a cofiltered limit of qcqs schemes with affine transition maps, Mathlib shows that morphisms to a locally finitely presented target factor through a finite stage, and that two morphisms agreeing on the limit agree at a finite stage. Missing: descending the objects themselves (curve, polarisation, group law, subgroup, level data) to a finite stage.

targets.target: The agreement locus of two finitely presented morphisms is representable and contains the original base after enlargement
targets.note: Equalizers of scheme morphisms exist, and into a separated target the equalizer is a closed immersion; agreement on the limit propagates to a finite stage. The combined statement is not formulated.

duplicates.note: Builds effective étale descent for schemes with a compatible relatively ample invertible sheaf, with descent of morphisms, sections and the polarisation. This is 0E's polarised-projective case, and it likewise refuses unpolarised effectivity.

Proves effective descent for sheaves, finite flat groups, polarisations and projective objects, keeping descent of a line bundle separate from descent of an object with it: the same object list as 0E.
Owns effective fpqc/fppf descent for the required objects in general.

targets.target: Weil restriction: for Z ⟶ S finite locally free and X ⟶ Z affine of finite presentation, the functor of Z-morphisms is represented by an affine S-scheme
targets.note: Neither library defines Weil restriction (restriction of scalars for schemes) or any Hom or Isom scheme (searched: WeilRestriction, restriction of scalars, HomScheme, Isom scheme).

targets.target: Special cases: tuples of sections of a finite locally free S-scheme; homomorphisms between finite locally free group schemes; the ambient schemes for the full-set, exact-order and full-level loci
targets.note: No representability statement for sections, or for homomorphisms of finite flat group schemes, exists.

targets.target: Compatibility of these representing schemes with arbitrary base change
targets.note: There is no carrier to state it for.

duplicates.note: Owns restriction of scalars for affine finite-type schemes along a finite locally free base map, by its functor-of-points universal property: exactly 0F's general Weil-restriction theorem.
Develops relative Hom and Isom schemes for the moduli proofs that invoke them.

targets.target: Relative Grassmannian of locally free rank-N quotients of the Hopf algebra of G/S: affine charts, transition maps, gluing, representability and universal property
targets.note: As the roadmap says, Mathlib has only the functor A ↦ G(k, A ⊗ M; A) of submodules with locally free rank-k quotient. Its own TODO list names the charts, the scheme over a base scheme and representability as missing.

targets.target: Closed loci cut out by the unit, multiplication, counit, comultiplication, antipode and Hopf-ideal equations
targets.note: Both libraries define Hopf ideals of a fixed Hopf algebra, and Tau Ceti identifies them with closed subgroup schemes over Spec R. Neither treats the Hopf-ideal condition as a closed condition on a family of quotients over a parameter scheme.

targets.target: The universal quotient's relative spectrum is a finite locally free rank-N subgroup scheme of G, compatible with base change; the parameter scheme is projective and finitely presented, and need not be finite
targets.note: No parameter space for subgroup schemes exists in either library.

duplicates.note: Constructs Grassmannians with their quotient universal properties and base change, and proves that invariant-subbundle equations are closed. That covers 0G's Grassmannian and closed-loci steps.
Realises Hilbert and Quot schemes inside Grassmannians: the general parameter-space theory of which the scheme of rank-N subgroup schemes is a special case.

targets.target: 1C: the variable-change group, its action on coefficients and the transformation law of the equation
targets.note: Details under 1C.

targets.target: 1A: projective Weierstrass models as proper smooth pointed curves, and EllipticCurveGeom S with its pointed local-Weierstrass atlas
targets.note: No scheme is attached to a Weierstrass equation in either library; only properness of Proj is available as an input. Details under 1A.

targets.target: 1B: the points dictionary over fields, local rings, trivial-Picard rings and arbitrary bases
targets.note: Only the affine-chart and equation-level dictionaries exist. Details under 1B.

targets.target: 1C (rest): pole sheaves π_*𝒪_E(n[0]), the positive-degree theorem, the pole-filtration construction, the action on the invariant differential, the classification of pointed isomorphisms and the Weierstrass-presentation theorem
targets.note: Only function-field Riemann–Roch inputs exist; the relative cohomology, the classification and the presentation theorem do not. Details under 1C.

targets.target: 1D: the scheme-theoretic group law by charts, and EllipticCurve S
targets.note: Only commutativity of proper geometrically integral group schemes over a field. Details under 1D.

targets.target: 1E: the cubic polarisation and elliptic descent
targets.note: Details under 1E.

duplicates.note: Identifies one-dimensional abelian schemes with Layer 1's elliptic curves using its Weierstrass-presentation theorem: the same carrier, reached from the abelian-scheme side.
Constructs the elliptic Weierstrass scheme over a field and compares its points and group law with the Weierstrass point group (1A, 1B, 1D over a field).
Derives Weierstrass equations from the ℓ(iP) = i ladder over a field (1C's fibrewise construction).
Owns cohomology and base change and Grauert's theorem (1C's inputs).
Constructs generalised elliptic curves and is required to prove compatibility with this roadmap's elliptic-scheme object on the smooth locus, so it shares Layer 1's carrier from the degenerate side.

targets.target: The projective cubic of W : WeierstrassCurve R as a closed subscheme of ℙ²_R, with structure morphism and zero section [0:1:0]
targets.note: Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.Projective is the equation in homogeneous coordinates, with point classes over a field. Neither library builds a scheme from a Weierstrass equation (the roadmap cites mathlib4#25983 for the affine model) or has ℙ²_R as a named scheme.

targets.target: Properness of the projective model
targets.note: Mathlib proves Proj 𝒜 ⟶ Spec 𝒜₀ proper when 𝒜 is of finite type over 𝒜₀ (an instance, name confirmed with Lean). Applied to R[X,Y,Z]/(F) this would give properness, but the model is not constructed.

targets.target: Smoothness of relative dimension one when W.IsElliptic
targets.note: Only algebraic stand-ins exist: on an elliptic curve over a nontrivial ring every solution is nonsingular (Mathlib), and over a field the affine coordinate ring is integrally closed (Tau Ceti). No smoothness statement for a scheme exists.

targets.target: Compatibility of the model with base change and with VariableChange
targets.note: Equation level only: variable changes act on Weierstrass curves over any commutative ring, compatibly with ring maps. The scheme-level compatibilities are missing along with the model.

targets.target: EllipticCurveGeom S: smooth proper π : E ⟶ S of relative dimension one with a section, Zariski-locally pointed-isomorphic to a projective Weierstrass model; base change and its functoriality
targets.note: No elliptic curve over a base scheme exists in either library. The closest carrier is Tau Ceti's AbelianVariety K, a proper geometrically integral group scheme over a field, with no Weierstrass atlas and no non-field base.

duplicates.note: Constructs, over a field, the smooth projective scheme of an elliptic Weierstrass equation with its section at infinity, and proves smoothness and properness: the field case of 1A.
Identifies one-dimensional abelian schemes with this roadmap's elliptic curves via the Weierstrass-presentation theorem, so it shares the EllipticCurveGeom S carrier.
Its proper flat families with smooth elliptic or polygonal fibres restrict on the smooth locus to 1A's EllipticCurveGeom S, and it names that compatibility as a milestone.

targets.target: Over a field with W elliptic, sections of projModel W ⟶ Spec K correspond to W.toAffine.Point, the zero section to infinity
targets.note: The affine-chart half is in Tau Ceti: for any R-algebra A, solutions of the base-changed equation give R-algebra maps from the coordinate ring (evalAlgHom), and conversely. Mathlib identifies projective and affine point classes over a field, and Tau Ceti identifies points with degree-one places. The projective model and the section at infinity are missing.

targets.target: Over a local ring, points as unimodular homogeneous triples; over a ring with trivial Picard group, the same after trivialising the line bundle
targets.note: Mathlib's projective point classes are defined only over fields, and there is no functor-of-points description of projective space over a ring.

targets.target: Over an arbitrary base T, T-points as a line bundle with three generating sections satisfying the cubic, up to isomorphism, proved by Zariski descent
targets.note: Mathlib has no functor of points of ℙⁿ, contrary to the layer's stated dependency. It has maps to Proj from generating global sections and the functor of points of affine space.

duplicates.note: Compares scheme-valued F-points of the elliptic Weierstrass scheme and their group law with the existing Weierstrass point group: item 1 of 1B.

targets.target: The Weierstrass variable-change group x = u²x′ + r, y = u³y′ + su²x′ + t: multiplication, inverse, action on the five coefficients, and the transformation law of the equation
targets.note: Mathlib has the group, its action on Weierstrass curves over any commutative ring and the coefficient formulas. Tau Ceti proves the transformation law of the equation over any ring, and over a field the induced isomorphism of point groups.

targets.target: Action of a variable change on x, y and on the invariant differential
targets.note: Tau Ceti's invariant differential lives in the Kähler differentials of the function field, and no variable-change transformation law for it is stated.

targets.target: The relative effective Cartier divisor [0], its multiples, and the line bundles ℒ_n = 𝒪_E(n[0])
targets.note: Tau Ceti constructs 𝒪_X(D) for a Weil divisor on a noetherian integral scheme of dimension at most one (an absolute curve), not for a divisor on a relative curve.

targets.target: For n > 0: R¹π_*ℒ_n = 0, π_*ℒ_n locally free of rank n, formation commuting with arbitrary base change
targets.note: The fibrewise count exists in function-field language: Riemann–Roch, and ℓ(nP) = n at a rational place of a genus-one function field. Tau Ceti also has absolute sheaf cohomology Hⁱ(X, M). Missing: the comparison with sheaf cohomology on a curve, higher direct images, local freeness of pushforwards, and cohomology and base change.

targets.target: Positive-degree theorem: for M invertible of constant positive fibre degree d, R¹π_*M = 0 and π_*M is locally free of rank d with base change; for d = 1 the evaluation section cuts out a unique section, compatibly with base change and fppf descent
targets.note: Only the function-field shadow exists: in genus one ℓ(D) = deg D for deg D > 0, and a degree-one divisor is linearly equivalent to exactly one place of degree one. The relative statements need the cohomology package of the Jacobian Challenge, which neither library has.

targets.target: Pole-filtration construction of a pointed Weierstrass equation Zariski-locally on the base, with unit discriminant; identification of the bases 1, x, y, x², xy, x³ and of the pole-order-six relation with the Weierstrass equation
targets.note: Not even the field case exists: Tau Ceti's own docstring names ℓ(nP) = n as the input for constructing Weierstrass coordinates, but no construction derives a Weierstrass equation from a genus-one function field.

targets.target: Classification: every pointed isomorphism of projective Weierstrass models over the same base is induced by a unique variable change, over an arbitrary base by descent
targets.note: Not proved even over a field. Tau Ceti's Aut.lean takes variable changes as the definition of isomorphism of Weierstrass curves, and its degree-one isogenies are not related to variable changes.

targets.target: Weierstrass-presentation theorem: a smooth proper relative genus-one curve with a section is Zariski-locally pointed-isomorphic to a projective Weierstrass model
targets.note: No relative curve theory exists in either library.

duplicates.note: Proves over a field that an elliptic function field has a Weierstrass equation via the ℓ(iP) = i ladder (Stichtenoth Prop. 6.1.2): the fibrewise case of 1C's pole-filtration construction.
Its acceptance instance turns ℓ(n·[0]) = n into h⁰(X_F, 𝒪(n·[0])) = n on a genus-one curve: the fibre of 1C's rank computation.
Owns proper-flat pushforward, cohomology and base change and Grauert's theorem, which 1C consumes for π_*ℒ_n.
Builds Rⁱf_*, cohomology and base change and Grauert's theorem over locally noetherian bases for relative curves, the same package 1C needs.

targets.target: Finite chart cover of E ×_S E on which the addition formulae are regular; the formula on each chart; equality on overlaps as scheme morphisms over nonreduced bases
targets.note: Mathlib has the homogeneous addition polynomials and a group law on nonsingular point classes over a field only. No chart cover, scheme morphism or identity of formulae as morphisms exists.

targets.target: Gluing the chart morphisms using the pointed-isomorphism classification, and compatibility with base change

review.notes: Checked all 290 targets of the 58 layers. Every one of the 213 distinct declaration citations was opened at its file and line in the pinned baseline and compared with the target: all exist, none is private, none is a structure field or axiom, and no cited file contains sorry (grep -c sorry is 0 in all of them). Nine citations name anonymous instances whose generated names are not in declarations.tsv (the four in Sites/Fpqc.lean, LocalFlatDescent, FlatDescent, Normalization, ProjectiveSpectrum/Proper); the source lines are exactly the declarations described, so the citations are sound. All 33 claims that a target is in the libraries were re-derived from the source, including the variable lines and instance hypotheses (IsSepClosed for exists_variableChange_of_j_eq, Flat+IsFinite+LocallyOfFinitePresentation for isLocallyConstant_finrank, IsReduced for ext_of_isDominant_of_isSeparated, IsAdicComplete+IsLocalRing for Weierstrass preparation and division); one was downgraded to partial. All 176 absent claims were re-searched independently by concept and by Mathlib naming convention over declarations.tsv and both Lean trees: effective Cartier divisors, relative ampleness, Weil restriction and Hom/Isom schemes, norms of line bundles, the Picard functor, Poincaré bundles, biextensions and seesaw, the Weil pairing, dual isogenies, Drinfeld and naive level structures, moduli problems over Ell, coarse moduli spaces, Tate normal and Legendre form, Tate curves, p-divisible groups, Serre-Tate theory, Verschiebung, formal-group height and Lazard, supersingular and ordinary, strict henselisation, excellent rings, Cohen-Macaulay and miracle flatness, regular schemes, Fitting ideals and flattening strata, Hopf-Galois extensions and torsors, scheme quotients by finite groups, Hurwitz's genus formula and Hilbert's different formula, GAGA and analytification, and prorepresentable deformation functors. Not one of them turned up; every 'absent' and 'partial' note I re-tested held. Three notes deserve highlighting as correct and load-bearing: deg [N] = N² over a field is present at the pin although the roadmap believes its supplier has not exported it (TauCeti.Isogeny.degree_mulByIntIsogenyOfNeZero); ker_baseChange_of_noZeroSMulDivisors_coker, which the 9E text names as if it existed, is in neither library; and the 5C claim that no roadmap owns the connectedness contract is out of date, since ModularCurvesPartII R12.4 and ComplexComparisonPartII C4 name it verbatim. All 104 duplicate references resolve to real atlas layers, none of them retired, and the load-bearing ones were read and confirmed; five were added. Layer verdicts are consistent with the targets after the corrections: every 'partly built' layer still has at least one present and one missing target, every 'not built' layer has none present, and no layer is bookkeeping rather than mathematics, so no 'built' or 'process' verdict is in question.
